intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed skiing abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski schools for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the iconic Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz for a breathtaking 8-hour panoramic journey through snow-covered Alpine valleys, frozen rivers, and dramatic mountain passes. A magical and comfortable experience for the whole family requiring no physical exertion, with dining service onboard.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais Alps

experiences.name: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Faulhorn
experiences.description: Experience the world's longest natural sledding run stretching nearly 15km from Faulhorn down to Grindelwald. Families can rent sleds at the top and race down thrilling snowy tracks through pine forests and Alpine meadows. Snow tubing parks nearby offer additional fun for younger kids in a safe, controlled environment.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Visit a traditional Alpine dairy farm in the Appenzell region to watch authentic Swiss cheese being crafted, then sit down to a hands-on fondue and raclette dinner with local farmers. Learn about centuries-old Swiss culinary traditions while warming up after a day on the slopes. A truly immersive cultural and gastronomic highlight for the whole family.

experiences.name: Ice Skating at Davos Olympic Ice Rink
experiences.description: Skate on one of Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rinks at the legendary Davos Olympic Ice Stadium. The rink hosts public skating sessions daily and offers skate rentals and beginner lessons, making it ideal for families. Surrounded by stunning mountain scenery, this is a quintessential Swiss winter activity that complements a ski-focused trip perfectly.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly SBB train from Zurich Airport to Grindelwald (approximately 2.5–3 hours via Interlaken Ost, costing around CHF 30–40 with a Swiss Travel Pass or half-fare card). Check in to Grindelwald Boutique Stay and get settled. Take a short orientation stroll through Grindelwald village to get your bearings, spot the iconic Eiger North Face, and locate key spots like the ski rental shops and grocery store (Migros or Coop) for budget meal prep.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Grindelwald village on foot. Browse the main street, admire the illuminated mountain scenery at dusk, and pick up snacks and breakfast supplies from the local Coop or Migros supermarket to save money throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick snack at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 10–15).
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pretzel at the train station kiosks (Brezelkönig or SBB bistro) en route — budget CHF 8–12.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta meal using groceries from Coop/Migros in the accommodation kitchen, or try a budget-friendly fondue or rösti at a local casual restaurant like Restaurant Onkel Tom (budget CHF 18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau Travel Pass or Grindelwald ski day passes in advance online for significant savings. Pick up a half-fare card at the train station if staying longer. Stock up on groceries tonight to reduce meal costs for the week. CHF 1 ≈ USD 1.10 — budget carefully.

day_by_day.morning: First full ski day! Head to Grindelwald First ski area — one of the most accessible and family-friendly ski zones in the Jungfrau Region. Rent ski equipment from a local rental shop in the village (pre-book online for discounts, e.g., Intersport Grindelwald — budget CHF 35–50/day for adult gear, CHF 20–30 for children). Take the Grindelwald First gondola up and enjoy beginner to intermediate runs. Families with young children can access the dedicated ski school meeting points here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First ski area slopes. Intermediate skiers can explore the longer red runs toward Bort. Families with young kids can enroll children in a half-day Swiss Ski School group lesson (book in advance, approximately CHF 45–60 per child for a group lesson). Take a mid-afternoon break to enjoy the mountain views from the First Cliff Walk viewing platform (free with ski pass access).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by gondola before 17:00. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a cozy café. Dry ski gear and rest tired legs.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at accommodation using groceries purchased the night before — oats, bread, cheese, yogurt (budget CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and thermos of soup to eat on the mountain — saves CHF 20–30 compared to mountain restaurant prices. Alternatively, share a budget mountain plate at a mid-mountain self-service restaurant (budget CHF 15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Cook dinner at the accommodation — try a simple Swiss-style potato rösti with eggs and cheese using supermarket ingredients (budget CHF 6–10 per person). Alternatively, visit Pizzeria da Salvo in Grindelwald for affordable pizza (budget CHF 18–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day ski passes for Grindelwald First cost approximately CHF 60–70 for adults and CHF 35–45 for children. Multi-day passes offer better value — consider a 6-day Jungfrau ski pass for approximately CHF 280–320 for adults. Swiss Ski School group lessons are more affordable than private lessons and ideal for beginners. Dress in warm layers — February temperatures at altitude can drop to -10°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Family-friendly winter activity day — try tobogganing on the famous Grindelwald toboggan run near Bussalp. Take the local bus up to Bussalp (included in many regional passes) and rent a toboggan sled (approximately CHF 10–15 rental). The 6 km run back down to the valley is thrilling for all ages and completely free once you have the sled. This is one of the best budget-friendly winter activities in the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Grindelwald Sports Centre (Sportzentrum) for ice skating on the outdoor rink — a fun, affordable family activity (entry approximately CHF 8–12 per person, skate rental CHF 5–8). Children especially love this activity. Alternatively, take a scenic winter snowshoe walk on the easy Grindelwald valley floor trails (snowshoe rental approximately CHF 15–20/day from local sports shops).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local event if available (check the Grindelwald tourist office board for weekly events). Otherwise, enjoy a relaxed evening at the accommodation with board games or cards — many budget stays have communal areas. Take a short evening walk through the village to see the fairy-tale lit chalets.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at accommodation — scrambled eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee (budget CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the toboggan hill — sandwiches, fruit, hot tea in a thermos (budget CHF 4–6 per person). There is also a small mountain hut at Bussalp serving simple hot meals if weather is harsh.
meals.dinner: Try the local Coop Restaurant or Migros restaurant in Grindelwald for an affordable hot meal — these supermarket restaurants offer daily specials including soup, main, and drink for approximately CHF 14–18 per person and are very family-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: The Bussalp toboggan run is best done in the morning when snow conditions are freshest. Check with the tourist office that the run is open — it depends on snow conditions. The Grindelwald Sports Centre ice rink is typically open daily in February. Snowshoe trails are well-marked and free to walk — just pay for the rental equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Jungfraubahn railway to Kleine Scheidegg (approximately 30–40 minutes from Grindelwald, included in Jungfrau Travel Pass or approximately CHF 30–40 return without pass). Kleine Scheidegg sits at 2,061m and offers spectacular views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Ski the famous Lauberhorn slopes — these are the same runs used for the World Cup downhill race. Intermediate and advanced skiers will love the long, sweeping red and black runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Kleine Scheidegg / Männlichen area. Families can access the Männlichen plateau via gondola from Grindelwald Grund (included in ski pass) for gentler, wide open beginner-friendly slopes. Take the famous Royal Walk — a flat, easy 30-minute panoramic walk along the ridge at Männlichen with breathtaking 360-degree Alpine views (free with gondola access). This is perfect for non-skiers in the family.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by train or gondola. Visit the Grindelwald tourist information office on the main street (free entry) to pick up maps and learn about local history. Enjoy a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at accommodation — muesli with milk, fruit, and coffee (budget CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from home to eat at Kleine Scheidegg with views of the Eiger. If buying on the mountain, the self-service section of Restaurant Grindelwaldblick offers more affordable options (soup and bread approximately CHF 10–14).
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a mid-budget dinner at Restaurant Alte Post in Grindelwald — a traditional Swiss restaurant with cheese fondue (CHF 22–28 per person) and raclette. This is a must-try Swiss experience and represents good value for a special evening meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch (Top of Europe) excursion is spectacular but expensive (approximately CHF 145–160 per adult). If budget allows, consider visiting on Day 5 or 6 instead of today — look for online discount codes or book the first morning train for the lowest fare tier. The Männlichen Royal Walk is flat and accessible for young children and non-skiers. Weather at altitude can change rapidly — always carry an extra layer.

day_by_day.morning: Budget splurge day — visit Jungfraujoch, the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m. Take the early first train from Grindelwald (departing approximately 08:00) to qualify for the reduced 'Good Morning Ticket' (approximately CHF 95–115 per adult vs full price CHF 145–160 — must arrive before 09:00 and depart by 13:00). Experience the Sphinx Observatory, Aletsch Glacier views, Ice Palace, and Snow Fun Park. This is the most iconic experience in the Jungfrau Region and worth the splurge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Jungfraujoch by 13:00 on the Good Morning Ticket. Stop at Kleine Scheidegg on the way down for a short ski run or a walk. Return to Grindelwald by early afternoon. Rest and recover from the high altitude — some visitors feel mild altitude effects. Light afternoon activity: browse the Grindelwald village shops for Swiss chocolate and souvenirs (Läderach chocolate shop offers free tastings).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the accommodation. Cook a hearty meal using supermarket ingredients. Share photos and highlights from the Jungfraujoch visit.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared breakfast before the 08:00 train — pre-packed bread, cheese, and fruit to eat on the train (budget CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: The Jungfraujoch has restaurants but they are expensive (CHF 20–35 per person). Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches — eating outside at the Top of Europe is a memorable experience and saves significantly. Note: food freezes quickly at this altitude.
meals.dinner: Cook a comforting dinner at the accommodation — pasta with tomato sauce, salad, and Swiss chocolate for dessert (budget CHF 8–12 per person total using supermarket supplies).

day_by_day.notes: The Good Morning Ticket is the best budget hack for Jungfraujoch — book online in advance as slots are limited. Children under 16 travel free with a paying adult on the Jungfraubahn with a valid family card (ask at ticket counter). Wear your warmest clothing — temperatures at Jungfraujoch average -10°C to -15°C in February with strong winds. Sun protection (sunscreen and sunglasses) is essential at this altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Final ski day — head to Mürren via the Grindelwald–Lauterbrunnen–Mürren route (approximately 1 hour travel, included in Jungfrau ski pass). Mürren is a car-free mountain village with access to the Schilthorn ski area (famous as the James Bond filming location). Ski the varied terrain including the long Schilthorn runs — the descent from 2,970m to Mürren is approximately 12 km and one of the best runs in Switzerland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at the top of the Schilthorn for the James Bond 007 experience and panoramic views of 200 Alpine peaks including the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau (cable car included in ski pass — restaurant visit optional, budget CHF 15–25 for a drink or light snack). Return to Mürren for a final afternoon ski run, then head back to Grindelwald by 16:00 to allow time to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Pack bags and prepare for checkout the next morning. Farewell dinner in Grindelwald village. Take a final evening walk through the village and along the valley to soak in the last views of the Eiger.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at accommodation — use up remaining groceries (bread, cheese, eggs, fruit — budget CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the mountain again — thermos of soup, sandwiches, energy bars (budget CHF 4–6 per person). Eat with views at Mürren or Schilthorn.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Grindelwald restaurant. Try Restaurant Pizzeria Alpenblick for affordable pizza, pasta, and Swiss dishes with mountain views (budget CHF 18–25 per person). Share a bottle of local Swiss wine or beer as a celebration.

day_by_day.notes: The Schilthorn cable car from Mürren to Piz Gloria is included in the Jungfrau ski pass — this is excellent value. The Lauterbrunnen valley en route to Mürren is stunning — look out for the 72 waterfalls visible even in winter. Saturday can be busier on the slopes — start early to avoid lift queues. Return all rental ski equipment today to avoid extra charges.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Grindelwald Boutique Stay. Store luggage with the hotel if checkout is before your train. Take a final morning walk to the First Gorge (Gletscherschlucht) viewpoint near the village — free to access from the road and offering dramatic views of the glacier gorge. Alternatively, enjoy a final hot chocolate at a village café and browse for last-minute Swiss chocolate gifts at the local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Grindelwald by train toward Zurich Airport or onward destination. The journey from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport takes approximately 2.5–3 hours via Interlaken Ost and Bern (or Interlaken Ost and Zurich HB). Enjoy the scenic train ride through the Bernese Oberland as a final Alpine experience — the views of Lake Thun and Lake Brienz from the train are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Zurich Airport or continue to next destination. Reflect on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final self-prepared breakfast using last groceries at the accommodation, or treat yourself to a Swiss bakery breakfast in the village — Bäckerei Grindelwald for fresh croissants, gipfeli (Swiss croissants), and coffee (budget CHF 8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack any remaining food from the accommodation for the train journey, or purchase a sandwich from the SBB train bistro or station kiosk (budget CHF 10–15).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight depending on departure time (budget CHF 15–25 at airport).

day_by_day.notes: Check train times the evening before to plan your departure correctly — Swiss trains run on precise schedules. The SBB app (Swiss Federal Railways) is excellent for real-time timetables. If flying from Zurich, arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Consider buying Swiss chocolate at the supermarket (Coop or Migros) rather than airport shops — significantly cheaper. Overall budget estimate for 7 days: CHF 800–1,100 per adult including transport, accommodation, ski passes, equipment rental, and meals if self-catering for most meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel time from airport (Zurich or Geneva) to Grindelwald is approximately 2.5–3 hours by train via Interlaken Ost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Grindelwald Boutique Stay around 15:30–16:00. Check in, unpack, and get settled. Take a leisurely orientation stroll through Grindelwald village to get your bearings — admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face, browse local ski rental shops, and pick up any essentials at the village stores. Arrange ski equipment rental for the week if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a cozy local restaurant in Grindelwald village. Try traditional Swiss rösti, raclette, or a hearty mountain soup to warm up after travel.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport — grab a snack at Zurich/Geneva airport before boarding the train.
meals.lunch: Light bite at Interlaken Ost train station café or a grab-and-go sandwich during the transfer.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Fiescherblick in Grindelwald — a mid-range Alpine restaurant offering traditional Swiss dishes like cheese fondue, rösti, and wiener schnitzel. Budget approx. CHF 35–50 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book ski rentals online before arrival to save time and money (shops like Intersport Grindelwald offer online discounts). Confirm boutique stay check-in time in advance given the afternoon arrival. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real!

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — First full ski day! Head to the Grindelwald-First ski area, ideal for families and mixed ability groups. The First zone offers well-groomed blue and red runs with stunning Eiger views. Beginners can take a ski school lesson (book in advance with the Swiss Ski School Grindelwald), while more experienced skiers can explore the red runs down to the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing, transitioning to the Kleine Scheidegg area accessible via the Grindelwald-Grund gondola connection. Intermediate and advanced skiers can tackle the famous Lauberhorn descent. Families with younger children can enjoy the dedicated kids' snow park near Grindelwald-First with gentle slopes and fun features.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a rest and hot shower. Head out for a fondue dinner — a quintessential Swiss Alps experience perfect for families.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or a local bakery such as Bäckerei-Konditorei Grindelwald — fresh croissants, müesli, and hot coffee. Budget CHF 10–15.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the slopes — try Restaurant Brandegg or Bergrestaurant Grindelwald-First for self-service Alpine lunch: soup, pasta, or a warm Wurstsalat. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte, Grindelwald — beloved family-friendly spot known for excellent cheese fondue and raclette. Budget CHF 40–55 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau Ski Region multi-day pass (available at the ticket office or online) — a 6-day pass offers the best value for the week. Dress in layers: base layer, mid-layer fleece, and a waterproof ski jacket. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — Alpine UV is intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Faulhorn — Take the First gondola up to Grindelwald-First, then hike or take the chairlift up toward Faulhorn. Experience the world's longest natural sledding run (nearly 15km) from Faulhorn back down to Grindelwald. This is an absolute highlight for families — the run passes through pristine Alpine scenery with breathtaking panoramic views of the Bernese Oberland peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the exhilarating sled run, warm up with hot chocolate in the village. In the afternoon, explore Grindelwald village on foot — visit the local sports shops, pick up Swiss chocolate and souvenirs, or visit the Grindelwald Museum to learn about the region's mountaineering history. Alternatively, enjoy a gentle snowshoe walk on the marked trails near the village for a more peaceful winter nature experience.
day_by_day.evening: Ice skating session at the Grindelwald outdoor ice rink (Sportzentrum Grindelwald) — a fun, affordable family activity perfect for the evening hours.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique stay — fuel up before the active day ahead.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or grab snacks from the village before heading up — alternatively stop at Bergrestaurant First for a warm meal mid-morning before the sled run.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Grindelwald or Café 3692 — casual, family-friendly mid-range dining with pizza, pasta, and Swiss classics. Budget CHF 30–45 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Sled rental is available at the top of the First gondola (approx. CHF 10–15 per sled). The full Faulhorn sled run takes 1.5–2.5 hours depending on pace and snow conditions. Wear waterproof trousers and gloves — you will get wet! Check gondola operating hours in advance (typically 08:30–16:30 in February).

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride (Day Trip) — Take an early morning train from Grindelwald to Interlaken Ost, then connect toward Zermatt to board the iconic Glacier Express. The 8-hour panoramic journey from Zermatt to St. Moritz passes through 91 tunnels, 291 bridges, and some of the most dramatic Alpine scenery in the world. Book panoramic car seats in advance for the best views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the Rhône Valley, Oberalp Pass, and Rhine Gorge (the 'Swiss Grand Canyon'). The train arrives in St. Moritz in the late afternoon. Spend an hour exploring the glamorous St. Moritz village before the return journey or overnight train back.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey by InterCity train from St. Moritz back toward Grindelwald (via Chur and Bern, approx. 3.5–4 hours). Arrive back at Grindelwald boutique stay by late evening. Grab a light dinner or room service upon return.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — pack snacks for the train.
meals.lunch: Dining car on the Glacier Express — a classic experience! The onboard restaurant serves a set lunch menu (approx. CHF 45–60 per person) with Alpine views. Book in advance through the Glacier Express website.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a Grindelwald village takeaway or hotel bar upon return — try a Bratwurst with bread, or a simple pasta at a local trattoria. Budget CHF 20–30.

day_by_day.notes: Book Glacier Express seats well in advance — February is peak season and panoramic car seats sell out quickly. A Swiss Travel Pass covers the train fare but a mandatory seat reservation fee applies (approx. CHF 33–49 per person). This is a long travel day — bring entertainment for children, snacks, and a camera. The Oberalp Pass section (around midday) offers the most dramatic scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Second major ski day, this time exploring the Wengen and Mürren sectors. Take the train from Grindelwald to Kleine Scheidegg and ski down to Wengen — a charming car-free Alpine village. The Wengen area offers beautiful long cruising runs perfect for families and intermediate skiers. More advanced skiers can tackle the legendary Lauberhorn World Cup downhill course.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the cable car across to Mürren — one of the most scenic ski resorts in the world, perched on a cliff with unobstructed views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Ski the Schilthorn area's wide open runs. Families can enjoy the gentler slopes near Mürren village while thrill-seekers head to the steeper off-piste sections. Return to Grindelwald via Lauterbrunnen valley train by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the boutique stay — enjoy the hotel's amenities (sauna or spa if available). Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Grindelwald with a focus on local Swiss cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay — hearty meal before a full ski day: eggs, bread, cheese, cold cuts, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Edelweiss in Wengen or a mountain hut near Mürren — try the Alpine macaroni (Älplermagronen) with applesauce, a classic Swiss mountain dish. Budget CHF 22–35.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Zum Dorfplatz, Grindelwald — traditional Swiss menu with seasonal specials, good wine selection. Mid-range pricing, approx. CHF 40–55 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: The Wengen–Mürren circuit requires train and cable car transfers — factor in extra travel time between sectors. Mürren is car-free and accessible only by cable car from Lauterbrunnen. Check last cable car/train times carefully to avoid being stranded. This is one of the most scenic ski days in all of Switzerland — bring a camera!

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — Take a morning excursion to the Appenzell region (approximately 2 hours by train via Interlaken and Bern). Visit a traditional Alpine dairy farm for a hands-on Swiss cheese-making experience. Watch authentic cheese production, learn about the centuries-old Appenzeller cheese tradition, and sample fresh cheeses and local products. This is a wonderful cultural break from skiing and highly engaging for children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Appenzell — stroll the colorful painted facades of the main square, visit the Appenzell Museum, and browse local craft shops for handmade gifts and regional specialties. Return journey to Grindelwald by late afternoon (approximately 2 hours). Alternatively, if the family prefers to stay local, spend the afternoon at the Grindelwald Sports Centre for ice skating, curling, or indoor activities.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve fondue dinner — celebrate the trip with a special cheese and chocolate fondue experience at one of Grindelwald's top restaurants. Try the classic fondue moitié-moitié (half Gruyère, half Vacherin) followed by chocolate fondue with fruit for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at boutique stay before early departure for Appenzell.
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a local Appenzell Gasthaus — try Appenzeller Biber (honey cake), local sausages, and regional cheeses. Budget CHF 25–40 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Glacier, Grindelwald — upscale-casual atmosphere perfect for a special farewell dinner. Excellent fondue, local wines, and stunning Eiger views. Budget CHF 50–70 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: The Appenzell excursion is a full half-day trip — start no later than 08:30 to maximize time there. Pre-book the dairy farm experience through the Appenzell Tourism website. If traveling with very young children, consider skipping the Appenzell trip and substituting a relaxed local morning with a final ski session instead. Purchase Swiss chocolate and Appenzeller cheese as take-home gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning ski session on the Grindelwald-First slopes — make the most of the last few hours on the mountain. Enjoy a leisurely ski with no rush, taking in the incredible views of the Bernese Alps one final time. Return ski rental equipment by 11:00–11:30 to avoid late fees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique stay (standard checkout typically by 11:00–12:00 — arrange late checkout if needed). Travel from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport or Geneva Airport for departure flights. The train journey to Zurich takes approximately 2.5–3 hours; to Geneva approximately 3–3.5 hours. Depart Grindelwald no later than 13:00 for evening flights to ensure comfortable connection time.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure — enjoy a final Swiss chocolate purchase at the airport duty-free. Reflect on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique stay — savor the last Alpine morning with a full Swiss breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Grindelwald village café before departure or at Interlaken Ost station — try a fresh Gipfeli (Swiss croissant) with coffee, or a quick Wurst mit Brot. Budget CHF 15–20.
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant at Zurich or Geneva Airport — wide selection of mid-range Swiss and international options available airside.

day_by_day.notes: Reconfirm return flight times and allow at least 2.5 hours at the airport before departure. Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) trains are extremely reliable — use the SBB app for real-time schedules. Consider purchasing a Swiss Travel Pass souvenir or final Swiss Army knife as a memento. Keep CHF cash on hand for tips and small purchases throughout the trip — not all Alpine restaurants accept cards.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Swiss Alps, Switzerland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed skiing abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski schools for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the iconic Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz for a breathtaking 8-hour panoramic journey through snow-covered Alpine valleys, frozen rivers, and dramatic mountain passes. A magical and comfortable experience for the whole family requiring no physical exertion, with dining service onboard.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais Alps

experiences.name: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Faulhorn
experiences.description: Experience the world's longest natural sledding run stretching nearly 15km from Faulhorn down to Grindelwald. Families can rent sleds at the top and race down thrilling snowy tracks through pine forests and Alpine meadows. Snow tubing parks nearby offer additional fun for younger kids in a safe, controlled environment.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Visit a traditional Alpine dairy farm in the Appenzell region to watch authentic Swiss cheese being crafted, then sit down to a hands-on fondue and raclette dinner with local farmers. Learn about centuries-old Swiss culinary traditions while warming up after a day on the slopes. A truly immersive cultural and gastronomic highlight for the whole family.

experiences.name: Ice Skating at Davos Olympic Ice Rink
experiences.description: Skate on one of Europe's largest natural outdoor ice rinks at the legendary Davos Olympic Ice Stadium. The rink hosts public skating sessions daily and offers skate rentals and beginner lessons, making it ideal for families. Surrounded by stunning mountain scenery, this is a quintessential Swiss winter activity that complements a ski-focused trip perfectly.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Allow time for baggage claim, customs, and private transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Grindelwald (approx. 2–2.5 hours via chauffeured Mercedes V-Class or helicopter transfer for ultra-premium experience). Check in to Boutique Stay in Jungfrau Region, Grindelwald. Settle into your suite, enjoy a welcome amenity from the hotel, and take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to get acquainted with the surroundings and rent or arrange ski equipment fitting at a premium ski shop such as Buri Sport Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant welcome dinner at the hotel's fine dining restaurant or at Restaurant Schmitte, a beloved Grindelwald staple offering refined Swiss Alpine cuisine with panoramic Eiger views. Enjoy raclette, air-dried meats, and local Bernese wines by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light bite at Zurich Airport's SWISS Business Lounge or a quick stop en route at a motorway service area with Swiss pastries and coffee
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte or hotel fine dining — multi-course Alpine menu featuring Bernese charcuterie, Grindelwald trout, and artisan cheese board paired with Fendant du Valais white wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Consider a helicopter transfer from Zurich or Bern for a truly premium arrival experience over the Alps. Confirm ski equipment rental appointment for Day 2 morning. Request early check-in if possible to maximize afternoon rest time.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day introduction to Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — begin with a private ski instructor session on the Grindelwald-First ski area. Warm up on the wide, groomed blue and red runs of First (2,168m) with spectacular views of the Eiger North Face. Private lessons ensure personalized pacing for all family skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing across the interconnected Jungfrau Ski Region, exploring runs above Grindelwald and accessing the Kleine Scheidegg area. Take a scenic gondola break at the Bergrestaurant First for hot chocolate and Alpine views. Advanced skiers in the family can tackle the challenging Lauberhorn red runs while younger or beginner members enjoy gentler slopes with the instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa session — enjoy the sauna, steam room, and heated indoor pool to recover muscles after the first ski day. Dinner at Restaurant Firestarter in Grindelwald, known for its premium grill menu featuring Simmental beef tenderloin, truffle fondue, and an impressive Swiss wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast buffet at the hotel — freshly baked Zopf bread, Bircher muesli, local cheeses, cold cuts, fresh juices, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant First on the mountain — Alpine soup, rösti with smoked salmon, and warm apple strudel with vanilla cream
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter Grindelwald — premium dry-aged Simmental beef, truffle fondue starter, and chocolate lava cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book a certified private ski instructor through the Swiss Ski School Grindelwald at least 48 hours in advance. Rent premium ski equipment (Rossignol or Salomon demo models) from Buri Sport. Apply high-SPF glacier sunscreen — UV exposure is intense at altitude even in winter. Lift passes for the full Jungfrau Ski Region are available at the gondola stations.

day_by_day.morning: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Faulhorn — take the Grindelwald-First gondola up and hike or snowshoe a short distance to the Faulhorn starting point. Embark on the world's longest natural sledding run, the legendary 15km Schlittelbahn from Faulhorn (2,681m) down to Grindelwald. This thrilling family adventure takes approximately 1.5–2 hours and passes through pristine Alpine meadows and forested trails with breathtaking panoramic scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the exhilarating sled run, return to the hotel for a warm-up break. In the afternoon, enjoy a guided snowshoe tour through the Grindelwald valley floor and lower Alpine forests — a peaceful, premium nature experience led by a certified mountain guide. Suitable for all family members including younger children.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — visit a curated Alpine dairy experience in the region (arranged through a local premium tour operator) to learn about traditional cheese-making. Follow with an authentic cheese fondue dinner at Chalet Restaurant Onkel Tom in Grindelwald, one of the most atmospheric fondue restaurants in the valley.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs benedict, smoked salmon bagels, Swiss honey and jam selection, freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Berghaus Bort mid-mountain restaurant — hearty Alpine bowl, homemade lentil soup, and warm Schoggi (Swiss chocolate) fondue for dessert
meals.dinner: Chalet Restaurant Onkel Tom — classic moitié-moitié cheese fondue (Gruyère and Vacherin), raclette, and Appenzeller cheese board with local Valais wine

day_by_day.notes: Sled rentals are available at the Grindelwald-First gondola station. Wear waterproof trousers and gloves for the sledding run — it gets wet and fast. The snowshoe tour should be pre-booked through a certified guide service. Children under 6 may need a sled companion. Confirm fondue dinner reservation 24 hours in advance as it is very popular.

day_by_day.morning: Full ski day on Jungfrau Region Slopes — today focus on the iconic Wengen side of the ski region. Take the train from Grindelwald to Kleine Scheidegg and ski down toward Wengen on the famous Lauberhorn race course (site of the World Cup downhill). Private guide available for the family to navigate the best runs. Stunning views of the Jungfrau, Mönch, and Eiger throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jungfraujoch — 'Top of Europe' (3,454m) via the cogwheel railway from Kleine Scheidegg. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and the eternal Alpine glacier. A truly world-class family experience and one of Switzerland's most iconic attractions. Allow 2–3 hours at the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by late afternoon. Enjoy a private in-suite or chalet spa treatment — couples massage or family aromatherapy session arranged through the hotel concierge. Dinner at a premium hotel restaurant or at Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof's restaurant, offering an exceptional five-course tasting menu with wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Continental spread with croissants, Swiss cheeses, charcuterie, yogurt parfait, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Restaurant Grindelwaldblick near Kleine Scheidegg — panoramic mountain views, alpine pasta, veal schnitzel, and homemade Apfelkuchen
meals.dinner: Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof restaurant — five-course tasting menu featuring Valais lamb, Swiss lake perch, seasonal truffle risotto, and artisan petit fours

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch tickets should be booked well in advance online — prices are premium but the experience is unparalleled. Dress in extra warm layers for the summit (temperatures can reach -15°C or below with wind chill). The cogwheel railway from Kleine Scheidegg to Jungfraujoch takes approximately 45 minutes each way. Altitude sickness is rare but possible — take it slowly at the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Ice Skating at Davos Olympic Ice Rink — arrange a private luxury transfer to Davos (approximately 2 hours from Grindelwald). Skate on one of Europe's largest and most prestigious natural outdoor ice rinks at the legendary Davos Olympic Ice Stadium. Private skating lessons available for children and beginners. The rink is set against a dramatic Alpine backdrop and offers a truly world-class experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Davos town — visit the Kirchner Museum (one of Switzerland's finest modern art museums), browse premium Swiss boutiques, and enjoy the elegant Davos Promenade. Alternatively, opt for a guided cross-country skiing session on Davos's renowned Nordic trails — some of the best in the Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Davos before the private transfer back to Grindelwald. Dine at Restaurant Kulm in Davos, known for its sophisticated Alpine cuisine and elegant ambiance. Return to Grindelwald hotel by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Swiss spread with warm pastries, seasonal fruit, bircher muesli, and barista-prepared coffee
meals.lunch: Bündner Stube at Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère Davos — classic Graubünden cuisine featuring barley soup, venison ragout, and Capuns (Swiss chard rolls)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Kulm Davos — premium Alpine tasting menu with Davos lake fish, Bündner Nusstorte dessert, and curated Swiss wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Davos is approximately 2 hours from Grindelwald — depart by 8:00 AM to maximize time. Pre-book private transfer and ice skating sessions. Skate rentals and sharpening are available at the Olympic rink. Consider combining the Davos visit with a stop at the Wolfgang Pass viewpoint for spectacular winter photography. Bring extra layers as Davos can be colder than Grindelwald.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — depart early from the Grindelwald/Interlaken area by private transfer to Zermatt (or join the route at an appropriate boarding point). Board the iconic Glacier Express for a breathtaking panoramic journey through the Swiss Alps. Travel through dramatic gorges, across 291 bridges, and through 91 tunnels with first-class or Excellence Class seating for the ultimate luxury rail experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey toward St. Moritz, passing the Oberalp Pass (2,033m) and the stunning Rhine Gorge (the 'Swiss Grand Canyon'). Enjoy gourmet lunch service on board in the panoramic dining car. Arrive in St. Moritz in the late afternoon — explore the glamorous resort town briefly before the return transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back from St. Moritz to Grindelwald (approximately 2.5–3 hours) or arrange an overnight stay in St. Moritz if budget allows. If returning to Grindelwald, enjoy a relaxed late dinner at the hotel or at Restaurant Glacier in Grindelwald for a cozy farewell-eve Alpine meal.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or premium packed breakfast prepared by the hotel for the journey
meals.lunch: On-board Glacier Express Excellence Class dining — three-course gourmet lunch with regional Swiss specialties, fine wines, and panoramic window views
meals.dinner: Restaurant Glacier Grindelwald — fondue bourguignonne, Alpine herb-crusted lamb, and chocolate Toblerone mousse for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The full Glacier Express journey (Zermatt to St. Moritz) takes approximately 8 hours — book Excellence Class seats well in advance as they sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Excellence Class includes a dedicated host, gourmet meals, and premium beverages. Alternatively, take a shorter segment of the route if a full day journey is too long for younger children. Bring cameras — the scenery is world-class.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning ski session on Grindelwald-First — a leisurely, unhurried ski run to savor the last moments on the slopes. Focus on favorite runs discovered earlier in the week. Take a final gondola ride to the summit for a panoramic farewell view of the Bernese Oberland — the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau in all their glory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return ski equipment and check out of the hotel. Enjoy a farewell Swiss chocolate and coffee experience at a premium Grindelwald café such as Café 3692 or the hotel lounge. Browse the village for premium Swiss souvenirs — Lindt or Läderach chocolates, Swiss Army knives, local cheeses, and artisan gifts. Depart by private luxury transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure transfer to Zurich Airport or Bern Airport. Allow ample time — approximately 2.5–3 hours before flight. Enjoy a final meal at the airport's premium dining options or in the Swiss Business Lounge if applicable.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell hotel breakfast — full spread including eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, premium cheeses, fresh pastries, and celebratory Champagne or fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Café 3692 or Bäckerei Grindelwald — artisan sandwiches, homemade soups, and Swiss pastries for a relaxed pre-departure meal
meals.dinner: Zurich Airport SWISS Business Lounge or Clouds Restaurant at the Prime Tower Zurich (if time permits before departure) — modern Swiss cuisine with city views

day_by_day.notes: Schedule checkout and transfer to allow a minimum of 3 hours before any international flight departure. Pre-arrange luggage handling with the hotel concierge. Purchase duty-free Swiss chocolate and luxury goods at the airport. Consider sending bulky ski gear home via a luggage shipping service (e.g., My Baggage or Swiss Post) to avoid excess baggage fees. Leave a gratuity for the hotel concierge team who arranged the week's experiences.
